<a id="page-import"></a>

## About this page

Brings your items over from another password manager or authenticator app, from the file it exports.

#### How it works

Pick the file with **Choose a file**. WM Pass works out the format itself and shows how many items it found, the first few names, and any it could not read. Nothing is added until you confirm.

It reads these files:

- 1Password (1PUX), Bitwarden (JSON or CSV), and KeePass or KeePassXC (the .kdbx database itself, KeePass's XML export, or KeePassXC's CSV).
- SafeInCloud's own database file (SafeInCloud.db, or a backup its app made), or its XML export.
- CSV from Apple Passwords, Avast, Avira, Buttercup, Chrome and other Chromium browsers, Dashlane, Firefox, LastPass, mSecure, NordPass, RoboForm and Zoho Vault.
- JSON from Avast, Enpass, Keeper and Psono, Proton Pass's JSON or unencrypted ZIP, XML from Password Safe and Sticky Password, and Kaspersky Password Manager's text file.
- Authenticators: Aegis, 2FAS, andOTP, Authenticator Pro (Stratum), Bitwarden Authenticator, FreeOTP+, LastPass Authenticator, Proton Authenticator and Raivo files, and a text file of otpauth links, one per line, which is what Ente Auth's plain-text export is.
- Google Authenticator's export codes, with [Scan Google Authenticator's code](/guide/settings/import/#action-import-scan-google), or a screenshot of a code chosen as the file.
- The Wi-Fi networks this computer has saved, with [Wi-Fi saved on this computer](/guide/settings/import/#action-import-saved-wifi).
- A CSV that WM Pass exported.

With nested vaults, **Import into** picks where the items go: this vault or one of them. The nested vault is opened for the import and closed again when you leave the page.

Folders in the file become folders here, matched by name. Attachments come along from KeePass, SafeInCloud and 1Password files. A KeePass or SafeInCloud database, or a password-protected Proton Authenticator export, asks for its password.

A login with the same site, username and password as one already in the vault is skipped, so importing the same file twice adds nothing.

The file is read on this device. Nothing is sent anywhere.

**How to export from your old app** lists the apps WM Pass reads. Choose one to read its export steps here, with a tab for each device; **Open on the website** has the same page with its pictures.

#### When to use it

Once, when you move to WM Pass, or to bring in one-time codes from an authenticator app.

#### Limits

Most export files hold your passwords in plain text. Delete the file once WM Pass has read it, and empty the recycle bin.

Encrypted exports from Bitwarden, Proton Pass, Aegis, 2FAS and Authenticator Pro cannot be read. Export them again without encryption. A KeePass database that also needs a key file cannot be opened here.

The importers were tested against sample files written from each format's published or observed layout, not against exports from every real app. Compare the count afterwards.

<a id="action-import-scan-google"></a>

## Scan Google Authenticator's code

Reads the export code Google Authenticator shows under Transfer codes, Export codes, with the computer's camera or from a picture, and reads the one-time codes in it.

#### How it works

Hold the phone up to the camera, or choose **Choose a picture** for a screenshot of the code. A screenshot chosen with **Choose a file** works too.

Google splits a long list across several codes. After the first, choose **Scan the next code** for each of the rest, then import them all together.

The codes are read on this computer. Nothing is sent anywhere.

#### Limits

The codes hold the secret keys of your accounts. Delete any screenshot of them once the import is done.

#### On Android

Scans the export code Google Authenticator shows under Transfer codes, Export codes, and reads the one-time codes in it.

Google splits a long list across several codes. After the first, tap **Scan the next code** for each of the rest, then import them all together.

A screenshot of the code works too: choose it with **Choose a file**.

See also [Import](/guide/settings/import/), [One-time codes](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-codes).

<a id="action-import-saved-wifi"></a>

## Wi-Fi saved on this computer

*Only in the desktop app and Android.*

Lists the Wi-Fi networks this computer has joined before and turns the ones you tick into Wi-Fi items, with their passwords.

#### How it works

The list shows each network's name and security, with **Tick all** to choose every one. On Windows and Linux they start ticked, apart from the ones already in the vault. On a Mac, where each password needs its own permission, none start ticked. Ticking a network that is already in the vault updates its item instead of adding a copy.

The passwords are read one network at a time, only for the ones you save, and the dialog ends on what happened to each.

In the item editor, **Pick a network saved on this computer** fills one network into the item you are writing.

Everything is read from the system on this computer. Nothing is sent anywhere.

#### Limits

- On a Mac, the passwords are in the System keychain, and macOS asks for an administrator's name and password before it hands each one over. **Always Allow** stops it asking again for that network. The Mac does not say which kind of WPA a network uses, so each is saved as WPA.
- On Windows, the list comes from the WLAN service. Whether Windows hands a saved password to a program not run as an administrator depends on its own settings. When it does not, the network is listed but not saved, and says why.
- On Linux, WM Pass asks NetworkManager through \`nmcli\`. A password kept in a locked keyring, or one that needs an administrator's permission, does not come back. Systems without NetworkManager, such as those on iwd alone, are not read.

#### On Android

On the phone it is called Wi-Fi saved on this phone.

Lists the Wi-Fi networks this phone has saved and turns the ones you tick into Wi-Fi items, with their passwords.

Android keeps saved passwords from apps. Shizuku, a free app, passes WM Pass the access a computer has over USB debugging, for as long as you allow it. The sheet says what to do when Shizuku is missing, stopped or not yet allowed.

A network already in the vault says so and starts unticked; ticking it updates that item instead of adding a copy.

In the item editor, **Pick a network saved on this phone** fills one network into the item you are writing.

On Android 10, Shizuku has to run as root to read the passwords.

See also [Import](/guide/settings/import/), [Kinds of item](/guide/how-it-works/#concept-item-kinds).
